VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security for its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, this is philosophically stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, first is to protect all the people and the entire territory of Indonesia.
Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions.
Likewise in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia fourth amendment, Chapter X.A concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government.
Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women Year 1999 it is stated that women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures of God Almighty, therefore they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded appropriately and proportionally both legally, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.
From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

Article 3
The best interests of the victim are all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, therefore the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.
What is meant by gender-based violence is actions based on gender relations that place women in a subordinate position to men and all actions that deprive children of their rights and freedoms.

Article 2
Number 1 Respect for the rights of victims refers to the fulfillment of the rights of victims.
Number 2 Gender justice is a process to become fair toward men and women;
Number 3 Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural activities, national defense and security and equality in enjoying the results of such development.
Non-discrimination is an attitude and treatment toward victims by not making distinctions based on age, sex, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.
Number 4

Article 5
Every victim has the right to report and receive assistance both psychologically and legally as well as to receive guarantees of their rights related to their status as a wife, mother, child, family member or as a member of society.

CHAPTER III RIGHTS OF VICTIMS
Article 4
Every victim has the right to obtain protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage and confidential handling both from individuals, groups or Government and non-Government institutions.

Because the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 Year 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), it is obliged to comply with these provisions.
Likewise in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia fourth amendment, Chapter X.A concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

The best interests of the victim are all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, therefore the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.
What is meant by gender-based violence is actions based on gender relations that place women in a subordinate position to men and all actions that deprive children of their rights and freedoms.
